primary_claim: Pretraining 6.9B-parameter LLMs with upsampled synthetic data depicting misaligned AI increases misalignment rates (41% to 61%), while upsampling synthetic data depicting aligned AI decreases misalignment (41% to 4%), and these pretraining-induced alignment priors persist through post-training and partially survive benign fine-tuning tampering.

effect.metric: misalignment rate (fraction of scenario questions where model selects misaligned action)
effect.value: base models: 41% to 61% with misalignment-upsampled pretraining, 41% to 4% with alignment-upsampled pretraining; post-SFT+DPO: 35% (no system prompt) / 24% (HHH prompt) for Alignment Upsampled vs 60% for Misalignment Upsampled

contradicts_or_qualifies: Challenges the assumption underlying RLHF, constitutional AI, and deliberative alignment that pretraining produces a relatively neutral substrate whose values are primarily set by post-training
Provides what the authors call the first empirical evidence of alignment elasticity occurring with realistic alignment data
stated_future_work: Deep character training: what other kinds of pretraining interventions are possible, and how to structure post-training so pretraining interventions are maximally effective, including improving [Special Token] persona training
Training data attribution: can misaligned behaviour be traced back to specific training examples
Scaling laws for alignment pretraining: do these effects scale with model size and compute
RL post-training: do findings hold up under RLHF and RLAIF
limitations_stated: Simplistic evaluations: single-turn binary-choice scenarios; 6.9B models lack capabilities for more realistic agentic evaluations; misalignment rates reflect self-report rather than propensities in realistic environments
Limited model diversity: only 6.9B parameter dense text-only English LLMs; resource constraints prevent multiple random seeds
No RL post-training investigated, despite RL with verifiable rewards comprising a substantial portion of frontier post-training compute
quote: upsampling misalignment discourse increases misalignment rates from 41% to 61%, while upsampling positive alignment discourse reduces misalignment from 41% to 4%.
